decidedBy: Essenthos, 2026-10-03, the occurrence read by Codex against the held Textus Receptus and King James wording and the existing Herodias-husband record; no person has reviewed this ruling
policy: The Philip named as Herodias's husband is kept distinct from the tetrarch named in Luke 3:1. A word is named only where this edition prints it; an edition omitting the name receives no invented occurrence.
source: Essenthos, the Textus Receptus Philip occurrence in Luke 3:19, read by Codex on 2026-10-03

rulings.why: The Textus Receptus names Philip as the husband of Herodias in Luke 3:19, as the King James reads 'Herodias his brother Philip's wife'. This is the husband already named in Matthew 14:3 and Mark 6:17, not the tetrarch of Ituraea and Trachonitis named in Luke 3:1. Nestle omits Philip here; this ruling is about the word the Received Text actually prints.
